title: Ambient Hom identification from a constructible realization and its transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite $E\subset\Omega$ put $B_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, and $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ valued in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ for the raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes, with its specified completed finite scalar transitions $S_{F/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the common-stage pair category of these $\mathcal C_E(T)$, with Hom groups the directed colimits over common finite fields [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $A=E_T,R_T$, let $\mathcal D_T(A)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of bounded objects whose cohomology sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which they are pro-etale locally finite free over $A$.

Use the specified tensor and permitted coefficient-passage internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Suppose $\rho_T:\mathcal C_T\simeq\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ is an exact equivalence with balanced finite-stage scalar comparisons and a symmetric strong tensorator $\mu:\rho_TL\otimes^L_{R_T}\rho_TM\simeq\rho_T(L\otimes M)$. Fix a permitted pair $M,N$ and its coefficient-passage Hom $H$, with right evaluation $e:H\otimes M\to N$. Assume $a\mapsto e\circ(a\otimes1_M)$ is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(L,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(L\otimes M,N)$ for every $L\in\mathcal C_T$, compatible with the specified finite rational Hom scalar maps.

Let $Q=R\mathcal Hom_{R_T}(\rho_TM,\rho_TN)$ in the ambient unbounded derived category [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and define $c:\rho_TH\to Q$ to be the ambient tensor-Hom transpose of $\rho_T(e)\circ\mu_{H,M}$. Then $Q$ is bounded constructible in the locally finite free convention of $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ and $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(R_T)$. For every $L$, the Hom bijection obtained from full faithfulness of $\rho_T$, the assumed transpose and the ambient adjunction is exactly postcomposition with $c$. The map $c$ is natural contravariantly in $M$ and covariantly in $N$, and its evaluation equation is $\operatorname{ev}_{R_T}\circ(c\otimes1)=\rho_T(e)\circ\mu_{H,M}$.

The actual $c$ respects signed symmetry and finite coefficient extension. In every tower the direct and successive comparison maps agree under balanced scalar multiplication and the specified rational Hom comparison; the identity extension gives the identity comparison. These are equalities of the evaluation-defined maps, not merely existence of some internal-Hom isomorphism.

proof.text: First put the two constructibility conventions on the same footing. The constructibility-identification clause of [lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone] says that, for $A=R_T$, the locally finite free description of $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ and bounded constructibility in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] agree, as object properties of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$; we use only this clause and its finiteness clause, not the realization equivalence. Hence $\rho_TM$ and $\rho_TN$ are bounded constructible in that sense. The coefficient is $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ with $\underline\Omega$ the finite-subextension-valued ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], exactly the algebraic-closure coefficient of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves] (not the ring $C(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of the localizing-closure convention). The scheme $T$ is separated of finite type over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, so $T$ is a scheme of the setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] used by that lemma. Applying [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves] with $\Lambda=\underline\Omega$, $X=T$, $K=\rho_TM$, $L=\rho_TN$ gives that the internal Hom $\RHom_{\Lambda_T}(\rho_TM,\rho_TN)$ of the closed relative module-object tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is bounded constructible. The zero object is bounded with zero cohomology and is allowed on either side.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 (ambient RHom restricts to the constructible six functors); the closure statement is the cited existing DAG result lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves

proof.text: Identify the internal Hom of Step 1 with the item's $Q$. Under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] the internal-module and sectionwise-module presentations of $R_T$-modules agree, and the forward functor preserves underlying sheaves, sections and restriction maps; hence exactness, cohomology and the balanced relative tensor coincide in the two presentations, and both derived tensors are the K-flat derived functor of that balanced tensor, i.e. the native derived tensor, which is symmetric by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. The site and sheafification universes are those of the item's ringed-site derived-category convention; no larger-index colimit is introduced. By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction] the recorded ringed-site internal Hom $Q$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is right adjoint to this native tensor, naturally in the tensor parameter; the internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is by definition right adjoint to the same tensor, so uniqueness of right adjoints gives a canonical isomorphism between them, natural in both variables. Bounded constructibility is invariant under isomorphism, so $Q$ is bounded constructible in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and Step 1's convention identification gives $Q\in\mathcal D_T(R_T)$. No discrete or continuous-map coefficient ring is substituted. Denote the ambient adjunction by $\Theta_U:\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes\rho_TM,\rho_TN)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(U,Q)$. Its counit is $\operatorname{ev}$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, ambient versus constructible operations; the all-coefficient closure theorem is the cited existing DAG result

proof.text:
Write $A=\rho_TH$, $B=\rho_TM$, $C=\rho_TN$ and $v=\rho_T(e)\mu_{H,M}:A\otimes B\to C$. Define $c=\Theta_A(v)$, as required. For $a:L\to H$, naturality of the tensorator gives
$$\rho_T\bigl(e(a\otimes1)\bigr)\mu_{L,M}=v(\rho_Ta\otimes1).$$
Naturality of $\Theta$ in its test object then gives $\Theta_{\rho_TL}(v(\rho_Ta\otimes1))=c\rho_Ta$. Since the assumed source transpose, full faithfulness of $\rho_T$, the tensorator and $\Theta$ are bijections, postcomposition with $c$ is bijective on $\operatorname{Hom}(\rho_TL,A)$ for every $L$. Taking $a=1_H$ gives $\operatorname{ev}(c\otimes1_B)=v$, the claimed evaluation equation. These equalities use the naturality and counit laws of the adjunction from Step 2.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.11 (adjunction convention); direct naturality calculation from the assumed source transpose and the ambient adjunction

proof.text: Both $A$ and $Q$ lie in the full subcategory $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$, by Step 2. Choose $L_Q$ and an isomorphism $t:\rho_TL_Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ using essential surjectivity of the assumed equivalence. Surjectivity in Step 3 gives $s:\rho_TL_Q\to A$ with $cs=t$. Put $b=st^{-1}:Q\to A$, so $cb=1_Q$. The two endomorphisms $bc,1_A$ of $A$ have the same composite with $c$, since $cbc=c$. Injectivity in Step 3 with $L=H$ gives $bc=1_A$. Thus $b$ is an inverse to this specified $c$. This argument uses only two constructible test objects, after establishing that $Q$ is constructible; it makes no assertion that constructible tests detect arbitrary ambient objects.

source.place: Agent-written two-test-object argument after Remark 6.8.15; inverse constructed explicitly

proof.text:
Let $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$ be morphisms between permitted pairs, and write $h=H(a,b):H(M,N)\to H(M',N')$ for the coefficient-passage Hom functor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The naturality-in-the-permitted-pair assertion of [lem-sf-adic-common-stage-hom-transpose] gives the evaluation equation
$$e_{M',N'}(h\otimes1_{M'})=b\,e_{M,N}(1_H\otimes a).$$
Apply $\rho_T$ and the natural tensorator. By the evaluation equation of Step 3, the uncurries of
$$c_{M',N'}\rho_T(h),\qquad R\mathcal Hom(\rho_Ta,\rho_Tb)c_{M,N}$$
are both $\rho_T(b)\rho_T(e_{M,N})\mu_{H,M}(1_A\otimes\rho_Ta)$. Injectivity of $\Theta$ proves their equality, hence the required contravariant/covariant naturality. The naturality of the ambient adjunction in its tensor parameter, as well as its target, is part of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction].

source.place: Lemma 3.4.11; direct computation of the two uncurries using the specified Hom bifunctor

proof.text:
For the symmetry convention put $e^{\mathrm{left}}=e\,\beta_{M,H}$. Symmetric monoidality of the assumed $\rho_T$ gives
$$\rho_T(e^{\mathrm{left}})\mu_{M,H}=v\,\beta_{B,A}=\operatorname{ev}(c\otimes1_B)\beta_{B,A}=\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{left}}(1_B\otimes c).$$
The last equality is naturality of the ambient braiding, whose signed complex normalization is preserved by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. This proves compatibility for the actual comparison in either evaluation convention: on homogeneous degrees $p,q$ both swaps carry the same sign $(-1)^{pq}$. Applying the inverse swap returns the right-evaluation identity, so it cannot select a different comparison.

source.place: Agent-written signed-symmetry calculation; ordinary symmetry constraints supplied by the cited native tensor theorem

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset F$ choose the common-stage representatives of $M,N,H$. Write $\gamma_Z:A_{Z,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{Z,F}$ for their specified scalar identifications after realization over $R_T$; for $H$ include the specified rational Hom comparison. Compatibility of the assumed transpose with this comparison says precisely
$$v_F(\gamma_H\otimes\gamma_M)=\gamma_Nv_E.$$
The tensorators here commute with the assumed balanced scalar identifications. Put $\kappa=R\mathcal Hom(\gamma_M^{-1},\gamma_N):Q_E\to Q_F$. By Step 3 and naturality of ambient evaluation, the uncurries of $c_F\gamma_H$ and $\kappa c_E$, after precomposing the tensor variable with $\gamma_M$, are both $\gamma_Nv_E$. Transposition is injective, so $c_F\gamma_H=\kappa c_E$. For $E\subset F\subset G$, substitute this equation twice: the composite uses $\gamma_{G/F,Z}\gamma_{F/E,Z}=\gamma_{G/E,Z}$ for each $Z$. For the contravariant variable, $\gamma_{G/F,M}^{-1}$ followed by $\gamma_{F/E,M}^{-1}$ equals $\gamma_{G/E,M}^{-1}$. Consequently bifunctoriality gives $\kappa_{G/F}\kappa_{F/E}=R\mathcal Hom(\gamma_{F/E,M}^{-1}\gamma_{G/F,M}^{-1},\gamma_{G/F,N}\gamma_{F/E,N})=\kappa_{G/E}$. These are the specified scalar comparisons: their associator multiplies scalars by $(g,f,e)\mapsto gfe$, so both evaluation composites multiply by the same product. For $F=E$, $1\otimes z\mapsto z$ and the specified identity Hom comparison give $\gamma_Z=1$, $\kappa=1$ and the identity equation. Thus the direct, successive and identity comparisons agree as maps, not just as isomorphism classes.
